/-!
# Erdős Problem 398

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/398](https://www.erdosproblems.com/398)
 - [Wikipedia: Brocard's problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brocard%27s_problem)
-/

open Nat

namespace Erdos398

/--
**Brocard's Problem**
Does $n! + 1 = m^2$ have integer solutions other than $n = 4, 5, 7$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_398 : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | ∃ m, n ! + 1 = m ^ 2} = {4, 5, 7} := by
  sorry

end Erdos398

findings.description: The docstring asks whether there are solutions other than n = 4, 5, 7, but the Lean right-hand side asserts that there are no other solutions. Thus a positive `answer` endorses uniqueness, the opposite of a positive answer to the docstring. The formal statement itself correctly matches the Erdős source.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/398 asks: “Are the only solutions to n! = x² − 1 when n = 4, 5, 7?” Erdős, “Quelques problèmes de théorie des nombres” (1963), problem 67, p. 129, likewise asks whether these are the only solutions. The file’s docstring instead follows Wikipedia’s complementary question: “Does n! + 1 = m² have integer solutions other than n = 4, 5, 7?”
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the Lean statement and change the docstring to: “Are n = 4, 5, 7 the only values of n for which n! + 1 is a perfect square?”

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether n = 4, 5, 7 are the only solutions of n! = x² − 1. Lean instead gives an equality of sets of natural numbers, using n! + 1 = m² with a natural-number square root.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Moving 1 across the equality over the integers is equivalent. An integer square root can be replaced by its natural absolute value, and a natural root embeds into the integers. The added boundary cases cause no change: n = 0 gives 2, which is not a square, and m = 0 is impossible. The known witnesses (4,5), (5,11), and (7,71) establish the reverse inclusion required by set equality. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, `set_eq_iff_erdos_source` proves the exact equivalence with ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ m : ℤ, (n! : ℤ) = m² − 1 → n = 4 ∨ n = 5 ∨ n = 7, without sorry dependencies.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/398 — complete statement, remarks and status, accessed through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/398 with HTML output after direct requests encountered Cloudflare.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brocard%27s_problem — problem statement, Brown numbers, conditional finiteness results and references.

P. Erdős, Quelques problèmes de théorie des nombres (1963), introduction and problem 67, p. 129: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-14.pdf (text accessed through https://r.jina.ai/https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-14.pdf).
review.notes: The sole theorem is mathematically faithful; only its docstring’s yes/no polarity needs correction. Both cited webpages still record the problem as open. Checked inferred types, factorial and set semantics, and answer scope. Lean computations for 0 ≤ n ≤ 100 returned exactly [4, 5, 7]; separate proofs checked the known solutions, excluded zero inputs, and established the relevant equivalences. The target file was not modified.
